facts.text: We need to add to the outline and include one plot idea for each of Jack, Sarah, and George seeing a dead relative and a possible future together.
The story should be written in the writing style of Charles Dickens.
The story should include rich use of language, vivid describing, and colorful characters.
The story should include intricate plot lines filled with suspense, mystery, and surprise.
The plot should advance through dialogue and description rather than narrative and commentary wherever possible.
The user wants to start with Chapter 6.
The user wants a 200-word transition about how the mirror comes to be in the house of either George's son or daughter.
The user wants an 80–1000 word chapter for Chapter 6.
The mirror is inherited by an elderly man named George who lost his wife tragically.
George becomes isolated and fixated on the alternate future the mirror shows him.
George struggles to let go of the alternate future and the memories it brings back.
George's relationship with his son and daughter becomes strained as his obsession with the mirror grows.
The user wants a 200–300 word introduction with at least 75% dialogue about how the mirror left Chicago and the grieving mother to make its way to San Francisco.
The mirror is to end up in the house of George's son or daughter in San Francisco.
The therapist can't actually believe Susan.
The husband forcibly removes the mirror in Susan's life.
The user wants a transition on how the mirror ends up in San Francisco.
The user wants an introduction to Katherine (daughter) and George (father).

keyphrases: plot ideas for Jack Sarah George
strained relationship with son and daughter

events.text: Write a 200-word transition for Chapter 6 about how the mirror comes to be in George's son or daughter's house.
Write an 80–1000 word Chapter 6 focusing on George inheriting the mirror and becoming obsessed with the alternate future.
Write a 200–300 word introduction (at least 75% dialogue) about the mirror leaving Chicago and the grieving mother to reach San Francisco.
Revise the plot so the therapist can't believe Susan and the husband forcibly removes the mirror; add a transition to how the mirror ends up in San Francisco and introduce Katherine and George.
